analyzer.description: One analyzer's lifetime counters, from the store's `counter` table - the rows `fathom index --stats` prints (ADR-004 §4.8).

computes.description: Misses: lookups minus hits. `puts` counts writes; this counts work.

hit_rate.description: `null` when nothing was asked: 'there was nothing to ask' is not 0%.

puts.description: Rows written, including a recompute after a hit.

cache.description: Cache state and the hit rate, over the store's whole life rather than one run.

blobs_left_unreachable.description: Blobs no cache row, `blob_ref` or `graph_chunk` names any more — the count §8.7's retention pass starts from. Eviction leaves them; it does not delete them (`reco-93w`).

cache_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes the `cache` table holds now — the number `cache.budget.mib` is the answer to (`reco-93w`).

cache_rows.description: Rows in the `cache` table now, across every epoch.

evicted_by_analyzer.description: Durable cache rows evicted, counted by the analyzer that wrote them — the "what got evicted" half of ADR-004 §8.6's observability claim (`reco-93w`).

evicted_bytes.description: Payload bytes freed by cache-budget eviction over the store's life (`reco-93w`).

evicted_rows.description: Durable cache rows evicted to stay inside `cache.budget.mib`, over the store's life.

payload_evicted_bytes.description: Bytes the in-process payload cache gave up to its ceiling (`rss.analyzer_working_set.mib`). In-process counters are flushed into the store when a run closes, so this survives the process that made it (`reco-93w`).

payload_evictions.description: Entries the in-process payload cache evicted to stay under its ceiling.

payload_refusals.description: Entries too large to fit under the payload ceiling at all, so they were never held. Non-zero means the ceiling is below the unit of work, which no eviction policy can fix.

finding.description: One diagnostic, always with its remedy: ADR-006 §10.3's 'a shrug is not a remedy'.

severity.description: What the finding costs the verb that printed it: `degraded` is a missing or wrong answer and moves the exit code of every verb that reports the index; `untidy` is housekeeping — reported with its remedy everywhere, and it moves an exit code only under `fathom doctor --strict`.

index.description: Index state: where the store is, what it holds, whether it can be trusted, what it still owes.

commits_retained.description: Rows in `git_commit`: everything the file retains. `commits` counts only the rows a ref still reaches, so this is the bigger number wherever a history was rewritten.

dead_commits.description: Retained commit rows no ref can reach — the commits a rebase, `--amend` or force-push replaced (ADR-004 §6.2). The remedy is the pruner, `fathom index --prune` (§8.1).

dead_files.description: `git_commit_file` rows the dead commits carry: what a prune reclaims with them.

dead_sample.description: Up to twelve of the dead commit ids, newest first, so a report line can name what it means. The set itself is `dead_commits`; this is its evidence.

commit.description: A commit row the store retains and no ref reaches.

dead_unjudged.description: Rows that are neither reachable nor provably dead: the store hit a break in the parent chain it holds, or had no ref tip to walk from. Never reported as dead.

dead_unjudged_reason.description: Why nothing could be judged, when nothing could: the store's own words.

repository.description: The repository at --root, from `fathom-ingest`'s health report. When `present` is false only `error` is filled.

remotes.description: URLs with any credential replaced by `***`.

root.description: Repository-relative or `~`-relative; never an absolute home path.

description: The sections `fathom stats`, `fathom doctor` and `fathom show` all print, defined once so three verbs cannot disagree about what 'the index' means. Owner: `e1.10`.
title: Fathom CLI - shared sections
